text: Remember, this was the summer and the hot sun is out, right?
So [[Bahira|بحيرى]] noticed that this caravan that's coming, there is a cloud that is covering the caravan, keeping it in the shade.
And wherever this caravan goes, the cloud is following it, keeping it in the shade, protecting it from the heat of the sun.
So when [[Bahira|بحيرى]] noticed this, he realized that this is something special. This wouldn't just happen for anyone. There is something special about this particular caravan.
And many caravans had passed by in the previous years, right? And he never noticed anything special about them, but this one he noticed something special.

So the caravan stopped in a rest area near that monastery. Of course, it's a long journey from [[Makkah|مكّة]] to [[al-Sham|الشام]], so they have to make many stops on the way. So they stopped at a point that was nearby this monastery.

And [[Bahira|بحيرى]], he wanted more information about these people in this caravan because he realized there is something special here, because that cloud is following them and protecting them wherever they go.

So when he saw that they stopped nearby for rest, he sent some of the people there in that monastery to go to that caravan and invite them for food—go to them and bring them back to the monastery, invite them for a feast of food.

So a few of the people from the monastery, they go and they reach the caravan, and they say that, 'You are invited to come to the monastery and have some food with us.' So those people—the people of the caravan, these members of the [[Quraysh|قريش]] who are with this caravan—they were kind of surprised that they were being invited for a feast,

because they had made this journey many times in the past. Every summer they used to make this journey, they used to pass by the monastery so many times, and they were never invited in for food or anything. So they said, 'This is strange, this is unusual. We're being invited for food today.'

'Okay, as long as we're invited, why don't we go ahead and have some food?' So they decided to accept the invitation. But they didn't want to leave all of their stuff, all of their goods that they had with them in the caravan—they just didn't want to leave it unattended.

So they decided to accept the invitation and go into the monastery to eat food, but they decided that they have to leave one person there with the caravan to watch over the stuff. And who was the youngest one there that they could tell to stay there and watch over the stuff? It was [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, the twelve-year-old boy.

So they said to him, 'Okay, we're going to go and accept this invitation and eat food. You stay here at the caravan and make sure that nobody comes and takes our stuff.' So [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ said, 'Okay.' He agreed, he stayed there. And the rest of the caravan, they went into the monastery to partake in this big feast that [[Bahira|بحيرى]] had arranged.

Now [[Bahira|بحيرى]], he invited them in for a specific purpose: to see the people and to see what was special about them. So he started serving them personally and looking at each one of them carefully to see if there's anything special in any of them.
And he didn't notice anything special in any of them. He thought these are all normal people. So he asked, 'Did everyone from your caravan come here? Did you leave anyone in the caravan?'

And then one of them said, 'Yeah, we're all here, everyone is here.' And then another guy said, 'No, no, no. Remember, we left the boy? We left that young boy to watch over our stuff.' And then a third man said, 'We left a young boy—we left this young boy, this orphan boy—while we are here enjoying food, and we left him with the caravan? No, this is very bad. We should call him as well to come and have the food.'

So they sent some of their people to go to him and to bring him into the monastery to have some food with them as well. So now [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, the twelve-year-old boy, he comes in. He comes inside, and [[Bahira|بحيرى]] sees him. And he sees that yes, this boy, this is the boy. There is something special about this boy.

So he sits down and [[Bahira|بحيرى]] serves him some food. And he wants to have a conversation with him. But before he starts conversation with him, he wants to just observe the boy a little bit, see what type of actions he has, see what is special about him.

So [[Bahira|بحيرى]] just serves him some food. And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, before he starts eating the food, he says, '[[Bismillah|بسم الله]].' And [[Bahira|بحيرى]] is amazed—look at this, he said, '[[Bismillah|بسم الله]].'

All of these other guys, when they started eating, some of them were saying, '[[Bismi al-Lat|باسم اللات]]', '[[Bismi al-Uzza|باسم العزى]]'—in the name of this god, in the name of that god, in the name of this idol, in the name of that idol. But this boy, before he eats, he didn't mention anyone except Allah: '[[Bismillah|بسم الله]]', and then he starts to eat. So [[Bahira|بحيرى]] is impressed—this is a sign.

Then he asks the boy, 'What is your name?' And the boy replies, 'My name is [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]].' Now [[Bahira|بحيرى]] is even more happy because in their scriptures, in the previous revelations, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is mentioned by his name. So when he said his name is [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], [[Bahira|بحيرى]] became more convinced, 'Yes, this is the boy. This is a special boy.'

And then [[Bahira|بحيرى]] wanted to test [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ. So he said, 'I want to ask you a question.' And he noticed, before [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ came in, he noticed that these people of the [[Quraysh|قريش]], when they want to swear, when they want to swear, they say...

...'[[wa al-Lati wa al-Uzza|واللات والعزى]]' or '[[bi al-Lati wa al-Uzza|باللات والعزى]]'. They would swear by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], which were two of their false idols that they used to worship. So when they would want to swear, make a statement and swear, they would say '[[bi al-Lat|باللات]]' or they would say '[[bi al-Uzza|بالعزى]]', and then they would make their statement.

So [[Bahira|بحيرى]], he noticed this. Even though he was a Christian himself, he didn't believe in any of this stuff, he noticed that this is what they were doing. So he wanted to test [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ in this regard as well. So he told [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, 'I want to ask you a question.' And he said...
'[[Sa'altuka bi-l-Lati wa-l-Uzza|سألتك باللات والعزى]].' He said, 'I ask you a question by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]].'

And then [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, when he heard [[Bahira|بحيرى]] mention [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], he said, '[[La tuhallifni bi-l-Lati wa-l-Uzza, fa-Wallahi ma abghadtu shay'an bughdi lahuma|لا تحلفني باللات والعزى، فوالله ما أبغضت شيئًا بغضي لهما]].'

He said, 'Do not speak to me in terms of swearing by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], because [[Wallahi|والله]], I swear by Allah, I do not hate anything more than I hate these two. I don't hate anything more than I hate [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]].'

Now look at this, this is actually amazing. [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ growing up in [[Makkah|مكّة]], growing up among the [[Quraysh|قريش]], where they all worship—or most of them worship—these two idols, they worship [[al-Lat|اللات]] and they worship [[al-Uzza|العزى]], and they worship other idols as well. And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is growing up in these households where these idols are worshipped. He grew up with [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]...

...and [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was from the people who worshipped these idols as well. He grew up with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]]—he's living with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] during this time even—and [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] worshipped these idols as well. So this idol worship is all around him, even from his own family members, yet still Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is the One who protected him from ever falling into [[shirk|شرك]], from ever falling into any type of association of partners with Allah. Allah protected him.

So he said, '[[Wallahi ma abghadtu shay'an bughdi lahuma|والله ما أبغضت شيئًا بغضي لهما]]. I have never hated anything in my life more than I hate [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], so don't talk to me about that.'
So [[Bahira|بحيرى]] is very happy to hear these answers, very happy. That was his test, and [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ passed this test perfectly.

Then he said, 'Okay, I won't ask you by swearing by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], [[sa'altuka bi-Llah|سألتك بالله]], I ask you by Allah.' Then [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ said, 'Yes, this is what I want, this is okay.'

And then he started asking him some personal questions. And every answer that [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ gave him increased [[Bahira|بحيرى]]'s certainty that this is the Prophet that we are waiting for. He is going to become that Prophet that we are waiting for.

So [[Bahira|بحيرى]] is very happy with all of his answers. He asks him some personal questions, he asks him some questions about what kind of dreams he has, and all of the answers increased the certainty of [[Bahira|بحيرى]] that this boy is going to grow up to be the Messenger of Allah that we are waiting for.
Finally, [[Bahira|بحيرى]] had one more request to [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ. He said, 'Do you mind, can you just uncover your back? Let me see your back, the skin on your back.'
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, twelve-year-old boy...
